118	## Market clearing
119	
120	The `carbon_market.market.clear(jobs, supply, ledger, job_id, key, at)` entry adds the new-market clearing ledger on top of accepted jobs and the versioned resource supply. The three paths, `job_id` and `key` must be non-empty strings, `at` a non-boolean non-negative integer evaluation moment, and the three paths must resolve to distinct real locations; any violation raises `ValueError` before any business file is read.
121	
122	The acceptance file and the supply file are read as one snapshot under their shared locks, together with the ledger's exclusive lock; the three locks are taken in resolved real-path sorted order so concurrent calls can never deadlock. Only each resource's highest version valid at `at` is considered, and region, residency, cost budget, carbon budget, deadline coverage and the candidate entries (`resource`, `total_cost`, `total_carbon`) follow exactly the `resources.feasible` semantics. In addition, each resource version's capacity is reduced by the work of every trade already booked against that exact resource version in the ledger, so concurrent clearings can never oversell capacity and bookings never cross resource versions. The remaining candidates are ordered by carbon intensity, unit cost and resource id; the first one is the unique winner.
123	
124	The call returns `(trade, created)`. The trade binds the job id, the evaluation moment, the work, the complete ordered candidate snapshot and a versioned selection (`resource_id`, `version`). A missing ledger is created only when the first trade is made; the trade, the idempotency binding (key to job id and evaluation moment) and the audit event binding the request key, the resource id and its selected version are committed together — ledger sections sorted by code point, compact UTF-8 JSON with non-ASCII written through and one trailing newline, written through a synced same-directory temporary file, atomic replace and directory fsync; a failed commit restores the pre-call bytes (or removes a ledger that did not exist).
125	
126	Replaying the same key with the same job and evaluation moment returns the stored trade with `False` without reselecting a resource, appending an event or rewriting a byte. The same key with a changed request, or a job already traded under another idempotency key, raises `ValueError` and leaves the ledger byte-for-byte untouched. An unknown job raises `KeyError` and no remaining feasible resource raises `LookupError`; neither creates the ledger. Missing input files or a missing ledger parent raise `FileNotFoundError` without leaving a ledger or temporary fragment. Invalid ledger structure, references, ordering or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`; other locking, read/write or sync failures raise `OSError`. The existing `market.match`, the `resources` interfaces, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.

128	## Dispatch commitments
129	
130	The `carbon_market.dispatch` module adds the scheduling-commitment layer on top of the clearing ledger, with four persistent, idempotent calls over one dispatch ledger (`version`, `decisions` sorted by job id, `idempotency` and `audit` sorted by key — compact UTF-8 JSON with non-ASCII written through, no negative-zero or non-finite literals, exactly one trailing newline).
131	
132	`dispatch.commit(jobs, supply, trades, ledger, job_id, key, at)` reads the acceptance file, the supply file and the clearing ledger as one snapshot under their shared locks together with the dispatch ledger's exclusive lock, all four taken in resolved real-path order, and creates the job's decision: it binds the traded resource id and version and the job's deadline, and starts `ready` with zero attempts and no owner or lease. The dispatch ledger is created only by this first commit. An unknown job raises `KeyError`, a job without a recorded trade `LookupError`, and a commit moment past the job's deadline `TimeoutError`.
133	
134	`dispatch.claim(ledger, job_id, key, owner, lease, at)` moves a `ready` or `failed` decision to `claimed` under a non-empty owner with a positive integer lease, counting one more attempt; the lease ends at `at + lease` and may not pass the job's deadline. A decision still held under a valid lease, or a lease end beyond the deadline, raises `TimeoutError`. `dispatch.finish(ledger, job_id, key, owner, result, at)` lets the current owner inside its lease record `succeeded` or `failed` and clears owner and lease; a non-claimed decision or an illegal result raises `ValueError`, a different owner `PermissionError`, and a moment past the lease end `TimeoutError`. `dispatch.recover(ledger, job_id, key, at)` returns a decision whose lease has strictly expired to `ready` without counting an attempt; recovering before strict expiry raises `PermissionError`. These three actions take only the dispatch ledger's exclusive lock and fail with `FileNotFoundError` when the ledger does not exist.
135	
136	All four calls return `(decision, created)`; replaying a key with an equivalent request returns the current decision with `False` and writes nothing, while the same key with a different action, job, owner, result, moment or lease raises `ValueError`. Every first-served key commits the decision, the idempotency binding (the complete request) and the audit event (request plus committed decision snapshot) in one synced atomic write that restores the pre-call bytes on failure, so no failed call leaves a half-state. Invalid arguments, nulls, types, structure, ordering, references or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`, missing inputs or parents `FileNotFoundError`, and other locking or I/O failures `OSError`. The existing `market.clear`, the `resources` interfaces, the reservation migration, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.

138	## Execution plans
139	
140	The `carbon_market.execution` module adds the recoverable execution layer on top of the dispatch ledger, with three persistent, idempotent calls over one execution ledger (`version`, `plans` keyed by job id and dispatch attempt, `idempotency` and `audit` sorted by key — compact UTF-8 JSON with non-ASCII written through, no negative-zero or non-finite literals, exactly one trailing newline).
141	
142	`execution.plan(jobs, supply, trades, dispatch, ledger, job_id, key, owner, source, at)` reads the acceptance file, the supply file, the clearing ledger and the dispatch ledger as one snapshot under their shared locks together with the execution ledger's exclusive lock, all five taken in resolved real-path order, and creates the plan for one `claimed` decision held by `owner` and still inside its lease — a decision in any other state raises `ValueError`, a different owner `PermissionError`, a moment past the lease end `TimeoutError`. The plan is numbered by the decision's dispatch attempt count and fixes the job, the traded resource id and version, the deadline, the owner and the lease end; one dispatch attempt yields at most one plan. An empty `source` (`None` or `""`) creates a `launch` plan whose steps are `stage` then `start`; a non-empty `source` creates a `migrate` plan whose steps are `copy` then `switch`, and the source must name a published resource other than the target whose residency list covers the job's residency regions, else `LookupError`. 143	
144	`execution.record(ledger, job_id, attempt, key, owner, step, result, receipt, at)` appends one step receipt — the step, `succeeded` or `failed`, a non-empty receipt string and the moment — to an active plan; steps advance only on success, a receipt naming anything but the next pending step raises `ValueError`, a failed step terminates the plan as `failed`, a successful last step as `completed`, and terminal plans accept no further receipts. Only the plan's owner acting inside the lease may record: a different owner raises `PermissionError` and a moment past the lease end `TimeoutError`. `execution.recover(ledger, job_id, attempt, key, at)` turns an active plan whose lease has strictly expired `interrupted`, preserving every recorded receipt; recovering before strict expiry raises `PermissionError`. These two calls take only the execution ledger's exclusive lock and fail with `FileNotFoundError` when the ledger does not exist.
145	
146	All three calls return `(plan, created)` and share one idempotency key space; replaying a key with an equivalent request returns the current plan with `False` and writes nothing, while the same key with a different action, job, attempt, owner, source, step, result, receipt or moment raises `ValueError`. Every first-served key commits the plan, the idempotency binding (the complete request) and the audit event (request plus committed plan snapshot) in one synced atomic write that restores the pre-call bytes on failure. An unknown job or attempt raises `KeyError`; invalid arguments, nulls, types, structure, ordering, references or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`, missing inputs or parents `FileNotFoundError`, and other locking or I/O failures `OSError`. The existing `dispatch` interfaces, `market.clear`, the `resources` interfaces, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.

148	## Execution synchronization
149	
150	The `carbon_market.execution_sync` module adds the persistent reconciliation layer on top of the execution and dispatch ledgers with one call, `execution_sync.run(execution, dispatch, ledger, owner, key, now, lease)`. The three ledger paths must be non-empty strings resolving to distinct real locations, `owner` and `key` non-empty strings, `now` a non-boolean non-negative integer moment and `lease` a non-boolean positive integer coordination lease; any violation raises `ValueError` before a business file is read.
151	
152	The first call for a batch `key` scans the execution ledger by job id and attempt and fixes the batch as exactly the terminal plans (`completed`, `failed` or `interrupted`) no earlier batch has already synced. A `completed` plan finishes the dispatch decision as succeeded, a `failed` plan as failed, and an `interrupted` plan recovers the strictly expired claim; the action moment is always history — the last step receipt's moment for a finish, the recorded execution-recovery moment for a recover — and a retry can never rewrite it. Each item is first persisted `pending` in the coordination ledger, and only then is the existing `dispatch.finish`/`dispatch.recover` interface called with an idempotency key derived stably from the batch key and the plan identity, so a crash re-entry replays the very same request. The item becomes `applied` only after a successful call or an equivalent replay, saving the returned decision; a failure records the public exception class, keeps the item pending and re-raises the original exception with its chain.
153	
154	The call returns `(batch, created)`, a fixed-order copy of the current batch snapshot and the first-creation flag. The same batch key fixes its first scan forever: re-entry continues the unfinished items and a completed batch replays without rewriting a byte; terminal plans appearing later require a new batch key, and even an empty first scan commits an explicit `completed` state with the full audit snapshot. An active batch may only be continued by its current owner — a different owner before strict lease expiry raises `PermissionError` — while after expiry another owner may take over without repeating any applied item. Before any advance, the dispatch decision's state, attempt, owner and lease are checked against the plan (as is a dispatch idempotency key already bound to a different request); any mismatch raises `ValueError` without advancing.
155	
156	The coordination ledger (`version`, `batches` sorted by key with each batch's items sorted, and an append-only `audit`) is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with non-ASCII written through, decimal integers and exactly one trailing newline. The coordination ledger's exclusive lock is taken first and held for the whole run, followed by the two input ledgers' shared locks in resolved real-path order — released before the existing dispatch interface takes the dispatch ledger's own exclusive lock per item — so concurrent processes lock in one acyclic real-path order and can never deadlock. Every commit goes through a synced same-directory temporary file, atomic replace and directory fsync; a failed commit restores the previous bytes (or removes a ledger that did not exist) and clears the leftover fragment. Invalid structure, ordering, references or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`; missing input files or the ledger parent raise `FileNotFoundError`; other locking or I/O failures raise `OSError`. The existing `execution`, `dispatch` and `market` interfaces, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.

168	## Live feasibility and clearing
169	
170	`resources.feasible_live(job_path, supply_path, signal_path, job_id, at)` is the dynamic counterpart of `resources.feasible`: the acceptance, supply and signal files are read as one snapshot under their shared locks (the three paths must be distinct real locations). Each resource contributes only its highest supply version valid at `at`; its region, capacity, residency and deadline constraints are unchanged, but the unit cost and carbon intensity are taken from the resource region's latest signal that is valid at `at` rather than from the supply version. A region without a current signal simply removes that resource; it is never an error. The totals, `max_cost`/`carbon_cap` exclusions and the ordering (signal carbon intensity, then signal unit cost, then resource id) follow `feasible`; each result entry carries `resource`, `signal` (the full frozen signal record with its version), `total_cost` and `total_carbon`, and an empty list means no candidate. 171	
172	`market.clear_live(jobs, supply, signals, ledger, job_id, key, at)` adds live clearing on top of the same clearing ledger used by `market.clear` — the call takes the three snapshot shared locks and the ledger exclusive lock, all four locked in resolved real-path order, and deducts each booking from the capacity of the exact resource version, counting trades made by either `clear` or `clear_live`, so the two pricing modes share one capacity pool and never oversell. 174	The replay and conflict rules mirror `clear`: the same key with the same job and evaluation moment returns the stored trade — static or live — with `False` without reselecting, appending an event or rewriting a byte; the same key with a changed request, or a job already traded under another key, raises `ValueError` with the ledger untouched; an unknown job raises `KeyError` and no remaining feasible resource `LookupError`, neither creating the ledger. The existing resource, clearing and README public entry points and the HTTP behavior are unchanged.

176	## Re-evaluation and migration advice
177	
178	The `carbon_market.rebalance` module adds the missing re-evaluation layer on top of the live signals, the booked clearing trades and the dispatch and execution layers. `rebalance.evaluate(jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution, ledger, job_id, key, at)` re-reads an unfinished booking at the non-boolean non-negative evaluation moment `at` and advises whether the job should keep running on the resource version its trade froze or migrate to a resource whose current version is cleaner or cheaper under the latest signals. The seven paths, `job_id` and `key` must be non-empty strings and the seven paths must resolve to distinct real locations; any violation raises `ValueError` before a business file is read.
179	
180	All seven files are read as one snapshot: the six input files under shared locks and the advice ledger under its exclusive lock, all taken in resolved real-path order. The retained item always uses the exact resource version the trade froze — a newer published version of the same resource never replaces it, even once the frozen version's own supply window would have passed. A migration item uses only another resource's highest supply version valid at `at`, never a different version of the current resource. Every item prices on the region's latest signal observed no later than `at` and not expired at it (a region without such a signal simply drops out), and keeps the job's regions, residency, deadline coverage, cost budget and carbon budget. Capacity is deducted per exact resource version for the trades of every *other* job, while this job's own frozen occupancy is never deducted against itself. Feasible items are ordered by signal carbon intensity, then signal unit cost, then resource id. The first item is the advice target: `keep` when it is still the current resource version, otherwise `migrate`.
181	
182	Advice is refused before any write, in a fixed order: a dispatch decision that has already succeeded, or an execution plan that has already completed, raises `ValueError`; an active execution plan raises `PermissionError` (the booking must not be re-decided while work is in flight); and an evaluation moment past the job deadline raises `TimeoutError`. An unknown job or dispatch decision raises `KeyError`; a job without a recorded trade or an empty feasible set raises `LookupError`; none of these creates the advice ledger. An interrupted or failed plan does not block re-evaluation; the record's `execution` field freezes `none`, `active`, `completed`, `failed` or `interrupted` from the plan with the highest dispatch attempt, and `dispatch` freezes the decision state at evaluation time.

185	
186	The advice ledger (`version`, `records` and `audit` sorted by idempotency key) is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with non-ASCII written through, decimal integers and exactly one trailing newline. Every read requires the on-disk bytes to be that canonical form; the frozen supply and signal references, totals, ordering, the current selection and the keep/migrate target are revalidated against the current snapshots, while the dispatch/execution states stay frozen point-in-time facts. Invalid arguments or ledger bytes raise `ValueError`, other locking or I/O failures `OSError`. The existing `resources`, `market`, `dispatch`, `execution` and `execution_sync` interfaces, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.

200	## Migration claim, execution and release
201	
202	`rebalance.start(jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution, advice, ledger, job_id, key, owner, lease_end, at)` closes the loop the reservation opened: it claims one recorded `reserved` intent — neither finished nor already occupied — and freezes the intent's source and target resource versions into a migration plan bound to an `owner` and a `lease_end` that must not pass the job deadline, with the step sequence `copy` then `switch`. The target capacity stays exclusively held by the intent for the whole execution. The eight paths, `job_id`, `key` and `owner` must be non-empty strings resolving to distinct real locations, `lease_end` a non-boolean positive integer and `at` a non-boolean non-negative integer start moment; any violation raises `ValueError` before a business file is read. All eight files are read as one snapshot under the same locking discipline as `apply` — the seven inputs shared, the intent ledger exclusive, all in resolved real-path order.
203	
204	Only an unfinished, unclaimed booking may start a migration, refused in a fixed order: an already `active` plan raises `PermissionError` and a terminal one `ValueError`; a succeeded dispatch decision or a completed execution plan raises `ValueError`; a claimed decision or an active execution plan raises `PermissionError`; and a start moment past the job deadline raises `TimeoutError` — none of them writes. An unknown job, intent or dispatch decision raises `KeyError`.
205	
206	`rebalance.record(jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution, advice, ledger, job_id, key, owner, step, result, receipt, at)` lets the current owner, inside the lease, commit the non-empty `receipt` of the next pending step — `copy` then `switch`, never skipped or repeated. A plan that is not active raises `ValueError`, a different owner raises `PermissionError` and a moment past the lease end raises `TimeoutError`. A receipt moment earlier than the plan start or earlier than the previous receipt raises `ValueError`. A successful `switch` turns the plan `migrated` and releases the source capacity the trade froze; any `failed` step turns the plan `failed` and releases the target reservation immediately, leaving the source trade occupancy untouched. Terminal plans accept no further receipts.
207	
208	`rebalance.recover(jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution, advice, ledger, job_id, key, owner, at)` turns an active plan whose lease has strictly expired into `interrupted`, preserving every recorded receipt and releasing the target reservation. A plan that is not active raises `ValueError`; a different owner, or a lease that has not expired yet, raises `PermissionError`.
209	
210	The three calls share one idempotency key space with `apply`: replaying a key with the same request returns the current plan snapshot with `False` and writes nothing, while the same key with a changed request raises `ValueError` and leaves the ledger untouched. Each first change commits the plan, its state, the idempotency binding and one audit event in a single synced atomic write. The first `start` upgrades the intent ledger to version 2 — every recorded intent is preserved and a `plans` section keyed by job id is appended between `intents` and `idempotency`; `apply` keeps writing the ledger's existing version. Capacity accounting recognizes the plan states: a `reserved` or `active` intent occupies both source and target, a `migrated` one only the target, a `failed` or `interrupted` one only the source. Every read requires the same canonical compact form and every commit the same synced atomic replace with pre-call byte restoration as the other ledgers; an unknown job or intent raises `KeyError`, missing input files or the ledger parent raise `FileNotFoundError`, invalid arguments, structure, ordering, references or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`, and other locking, read/write or sync failures raise `OSError`. The existing `serve`, HTTP and other public interfaces are unchanged.
211	
212	## Terminal settlement and the current binding
213	
214	`rebalance.settle(jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution, advice, ledger, settlements, job_id, plan_key, key, at)` turns a terminal migration plan into the job's durable current occupancy in one *independent* settlement ledger — the trade, dispatch, execution, advice and intent ledgers are never rewritten. The nine paths are the eight lifecycle paths plus the settlement ledger; they, `job_id`, `plan_key` and `key` must be non-empty strings resolving to distinct real locations and `at` a non-boolean non-negative integer settlement moment, all checked before a business file is read. `plan_key` is the idempotency key of the `start` request that created the plan. The eight inputs are read as one snapshot under shared locks and the settlement ledger under its exclusive lock, all nine taken in resolved real-path order.
215	
216	Only a terminal plan settles. An `active` plan raises `PermissionError` and creates no record; a missing job, intent or plan, or a `plan_key` that is not the plan's start key, raises `KeyError`. A settlement moment earlier than the terminal evidence — the last step receipt, or the recorded recovery moment for an `interrupted` plan — raises `ValueError`; a legitimate late recovery whose settlement runs past the job deadline is still accepted, so no deadline timeout is enforced. Contradictory terminal evidence, the same key carrying a changed request, another key settling the same migration, a broken running generation or contradictory snapshot references raise `ValueError`.
217	
218	A `migrated` plan confirms the target version as the current occupancy (`active`) and records the source version as the previous-generation binding; a `failed` or `interrupted` plan forms a compensation (`compensated`): the current occupancy stays on the source version and the target reservation stays released. The record freezes, in order, `job_id`, `plan_key`, the continuous running `generation` (the immutable trade is generation 0, the settlement generation 1), the source terminal state `migration`, the `before` and `after` resource selections (`resource_id`/`version`), the settlement moment `at`, the `state` (`pending`, `active`, `compensated`) and `audit` — the sorted, deduplicated idempotency keys of every intent-ledger action the migration committed (reservation, claim, step receipts and recovery).
219	
220	The first request first durably writes `pending` — record, idempotency binding and audit event in one synced atomic write — and only then advances the record to `active` or `compensated` in a second synced atomic write. If the process dies after the pending write, re-entering with the same key and same request resumes the unfinished finalization, completes it and still returns the record with `True`, never repeating a committed occupancy, generation or audit action; the pending bytes are the rollback base for the final write, so a failed finalization leaves a resumable pending settlement rather than restoring the pre-call bytes. Only an already completed same-key same-request call returns the current record with `False` and writes no new byte; the same key with a changed request raises `ValueError` and leaves every file untouched.
221	
222	`rebalance.current(jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution, advice, ledger, settlements, job_id)` is a strictly read-only view of the job's latest resource binding for later dispatch and execution: all nine paths are read under shared locks and nothing is created or written. A settled job returns the settlement's current selection — the target version for an `active` settlement, the source version for a `compensated` one — together with its `generation`, `state` and settlement moment; a job without a completed settlement returns the immutable version its trade froze with `generation` 0 and state `traded`. An unknown job raises `KeyError` and an accepted job without a trade raises `LookupError`.
223	
224	The settlement ledger (`version`, `records` and `idempotency` and `audit`, all keyed by idempotency key in code-point order) is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with non-ASCII written through, no negative-zero or non-finite number literals and exactly one trailing newline. Every read revalidates the plan reference, the start association, the before/after selections, the terminal moment ordering and the audit association against the current snapshots. Commits go through a synced same-directory temporary file, an atomic replace and a directory fsync, restoring the pre-call bytes (or the resumable pending bytes) on failure; a missing ledger parent raises `FileNotFoundError` without creating the ledger. Invalid arguments, structure, ordering, references or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`; other locking, read/write or sync failures raise `OSError`. The existing serving, HTTP and all other public interfaces are unchanged.
225	
226	## Test
227	
228	```bash
229	python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
230	```
